name: infer
description: One aggregator over every model-inference router that settles in crypto and asks for no documents — an OpenRouter over the routers. Six catalogs (NanoGPT, Venice, PPQ, Chutes, io.net, OpenRouter) are fetched at once and merged into one market: ~1,350 offerings of ~1,120 distinct models, text and image and audio and video and embeddings, one row per model with every router that serves it ranked cheapest first. The hard part is not the fan-out, it is that no two routers publish prices in the same unit — and two of them use the SAME KEY NAME for a per-token price and a per-million-token one, so a normalizer that sniffs field names mis-ranks a router by a factor of a million and silently never routes to it. Units are therefore declared by each adapter, never inferred, and everything downstream is USD per million tokens. What that buys is measurable: 217 models are served by more than one no-KYC router and the spread between dearest and cheapest reaches 5.6x for identical weights. Calls route to the cheapest funded router and fail over to the next when one refuses; each answer carries a receipt naming who served it, what it actually cost from the usage they reported, and what the catalog estimated, so a router billing off its own published prices shows up as drift in the ledger. Settlement is crypto and runs in the background, disarmed by default: the watcher prices top-ups and files them as proposals, and arming it to move funds unattended takes confirm=true plus a rail and a 24h cap. Private keys never enter this module — transfers are handed to the eth, solana or near modules, which hold them. Still carries both older halves: the temperature-0 receipts board, and the ONNX optimizer for when the cheapest router is no router at all.

binary.local: onnxruntime — CPU, plus any execution provider this build ships
binary.browser: onnxruntime-web — wasm + SIMD, threads when the page is cross-origin isolated, WebGPU where available
binary.why: one file, two runtimes, no second conversion — the bytes benchmarked here are the bytes the browser runs
binary.verified: a fused model was loaded from /blob and run in onnxruntime-web on 2026-08-29: contrib ops (FusedConv, BiasGelu) ran, com.microsoft.nchwc.Conv did not

passes.slim: strip doc strings, training info and unused initializers (lossless)
passes.shapes: shape inference, so every intermediate tensor is annotated (lossless)
passes.basic: constant folding, dead node and redundant cast/identity elimination (lossless)
passes.extended: basic + operator fusion: Conv+BN, MatMul+Add, GELU, attention (lossless; emits onnxruntime contrib ops, which the browser wasm backend does register)
passes.all: extended + layout transforms for the CPU that ran them (lossless, and genuinely unloadable in a browser: com.microsoft.nchwc.*)
passes.fp16: half-precision weights with fp32 inputs and outputs kept (lossy, ~2x smaller)
passes.int8: dynamic int8 weight quantization, no calibration data needed (lossy, ~4x smaller)
passes.uint8: the same in uint8 — some kernels only have a fast path for one of the two

state: ~/.mod/infer/ (models/<sha256>.onnx, registry.json, browser.json, router-catalog.json, router-ledger.jsonl, router-keys.json 0600, settle.json, settle-addresses.json 0600, settle-proposals.jsonl, zoo/<source>.jsonl + .state.json)

endpoints.app: GET /infer — Next.js console on app_port 3820; this path on the API port answers with the route map
endpoints.blob: GET /blob/:id — the raw .onnx bytes, what the browser fetches
endpoints.optimize: POST /optimize {model, passes?, batch?, runs?, samples?, tol?}
endpoints.compare: POST /compare {model, passes?} — every pass side by side
endpoints.examples: POST /examples {which?} — plant every builtin architecture (38), or the named ones
endpoints.report: POST /report {model, ms, ...} — record what a browser measured
endpoints.reports: GET /reports?model= — browser numbers next to local ones
endpoints.router: GET /router — every router and the terms it trades on
endpoints.router_models: GET /router/models?q=&input=&output=&coin=&kyc=&max_usd=&min_context=&multimodal=&free=&sort=&limit= — one row per model, every router that serves it, cheapest first
endpoints.router_modalities: GET /router/modalities — what the registry can do, counted
endpoints.router_chat: POST /router/chat {model, prompt|messages, require?, confirm?} — route, call, fail over
endpoints.router_spend: GET /router/spend — per-router cost, latency and billing drift
endpoints.settle: GET /settle — watcher state, arming, caps, 24h spend
endpoints.settle_balances: GET /settle/balances — what each funded router has left
endpoints.settle_rails: GET /settle/rails — which chain modules are reachable
endpoints.settle_policy: GET|POST /settle/policy {armed, rail, coin, floor_usd, topup_usd, daily_cap_usd, confirm}
endpoints.settle_sweep: POST /settle/sweep — one pass: read balances, propose or execute
endpoints.settle_pay: POST /settle/pay {proposal|provider, usd, address?, rail, coin, confirm}
endpoints.settle_start: POST /settle/start — run the sweep on a timer
endpoints.zoo: GET /zoo — every model source, its count and crawl state
endpoints.zoo_models: GET /zoo/models?q=&source=&domain=&task=&author=&local=&max_bytes=&sort=&limit=&offset= — search every source at once, with facets
endpoints.zoo_model: GET /zoo/model?key= — one row, every file with its size
endpoints.zoo_scrape: POST /zoo/scrape {sources?, fresh?} — crawl in the background, resumable
endpoints.zoo_plant: POST /zoo/plant {key, file?, name?, weights?} — download/build into the store

backend: python: http.server + onnx + onnxruntime (torch only for export), in src/; console: Next.js 14 in src/app, basePath /infer, /_api proxied to the python port

env.PORT: port for API, console and MCP (default 50820)
env.INFER_SPEND_USD: per-call spend guard for the router (default 0.50)
env.INFER_CATALOG_TTL: seconds a merged catalog stays fresh (default 900)
env.INFER_ZOO_TTL: seconds before a remote zoo source is re-crawled on start (default 604800; 0 = never automatically)
env.INFER_ZOO_GITHUB: extra GitHub repos to crawl for .onnx files: owner/repo@branch,…
env.HF_TOKEN: optional — raises the HuggingFace rate limit and opens gated repos
env.GITHUB_TOKEN: optional — 60 → 5,000 GitHub API calls an hour

auth.writes: open on loopback for models and the catalog; settlement is gated by its own arming and confirm flags rather than by a token, because the thing being protected is funds leaving a wallet this module does not hold

halves.router: every crypto-settled, no-KYC inference router as one multimodal catalog, routed by price and paid in the background
halves.proofs: post what a model said at temperature 0, hash it, sign it, publish it, and let anyone re-run the question
halves.optimize: ONNX in, a smaller and faster ONNX out, running unchanged here and in a browser tab
halves.zoo: every ONNX model this box can find — builtin, onnx-tests, torchvision, GitHub, HuggingFace, ModelScope, Kaggle — one search, one click to plant

routers.nanogpt: kyc none, no account at all; XMR/BTC/ETH/USDC/LTC/SOL/XNO; 601 models
routers.venice: kyc none; VVV/USDC/ETH/BTC, quotes a DIEM column; 362 models incl. image, TTS, embeddings
routers.ppq: kyc none, key bought with crypto; BTC/ETH/USDC/SOL; 369 models
routers.chutes: kyc none, Bittensor-native; TAO/USDC; TEE-attested chutes
routers.ionet: kyc account, Solana-native; IO/SOL/USDC; publishes measured latency
routers.openrouter: kyc account, no documents; USDC on Base; 447 models, the yardstick

price_units.canonical: USD per million tokens, everywhere downstream
price_units.per_million_tokens: nanogpt (declares its own unit), ppq, venice, chutes
price_units.trap: openrouter and chutes both publish `pricing.prompt`; openrouter means per-token and chutes means per-million. Units are declared by the adapter, never sniffed from the key name.

settlement.default: disarmed — the watcher files proposals, nothing moves
settlement.rails: eth :50730, solana :50710, near :50910 — each holds its own key
settlement.guards: per-top-up size cap (4x configured), rolling 24h ceiling, deposit address must be on file
settlement.spend_guard: INFER_SPEND_USD (default 0.50); an unpriced model counts as OVER the limit

zoo.what: every place an .onnx can come from, as one searchable catalog

sources.builtin: 38 architectures built here (torch + onnx.helper) — no network
sources.onnx-tests: ~1,900 conformance models shipped inside the onnx wheel — no network
sources.torchvision: 121 registered architectures, exported on plant — no network unless weights=DEFAULT
sources.github: the ONNX Model Zoo (onnx/models, ~2,300 files) + INFER_ZOO_GITHUB repos
sources.modelscope: every repo whose libraries include onnx (~7,300)
sources.kaggle: every model instance whose framework is ONNX

zoo.rate_limits: read from each server (HF `ratelimit: r=;t=` header, Retry-After); never guessed
zoo.resume: pages are appended to ~/.mod/infer/zoo/<source>.partial.jsonl with the cursor in <source>.state.json; a restart resumes, a re-crawl swaps in only when complete
zoo.external_data: weights named by the graph are fetched and folded inline — one blob per model
